nv_weakness_wall.blurb: A limestone sport wall on the Cathedral Rock cliff above Kyle Canyon, high in the Spring Mountains west of Las Vegas at roughly 8,100 feet. Eleven routes, nearly all bolted, start at an easy 5.7 and top out in the low 5.12s, with most of the lines falling between 5.9 and 5.11. The stone is middling in quality and decorated with chert rails. The walk in is a demanding hike with some route-finding, so the wall tends to be quiet and solitary rather than a crowd scene.

nv_bill_s_boulder.blurb: A sandstone boulder at the western start of the East Cluster, part of the Kraft Boulders in Calico Basin near Las Vegas. It holds eleven problems with a lopsided spread: a handful of easy to moderate lines from V1 to V3, a few in the V6 to V7 range, and then a V9 and a V12 roof testpiece for the strong. It is the second-largest boulder in its cluster, and the cluster itself is a loose scatter of rocks stretching east toward a famous neighbor, a few minutes further along the main trail.

nv_yin_and_yang_cliff.blurb: A pocket-sized sandstone cliff, about 35 feet high, tucked behind Kraft Mountain in Calico Basin outside Las Vegas. All eleven lines are traditional, so bring a rack: they run from an easy scramble-grade start through the 5.7 to 5.9 range, then a cluster at 5.10 and a couple of 5.11s. Two good cracks give the cliff its reputation and its steady stream of visitors. It catches sun in the morning and falls into shade by afternoon. The hike in takes roughly half an hour.

nv_playground_aka_the_mall_the.blurb: A south-facing sandstone crag on Kraft Mountain in Calico Basin, near Las Vegas, with eleven routes split between bolted sport lines and gear-protected trad. Grades are concentrated at 5.10 and 5.11, with a single 5.9 on the easy end and one 5.12 at the top. Because the wall gets sun for most of the day, it is a sensible winter choice. Despite several quality lines it sees little traffic. The trail from the lot heads toward the boulders, then climbs to a gap in the cliff band at the eastern end of the mountain.

nv_main_cave.blurb: A limestone cave at about 8,000 feet on Mount Charleston, inside The Subway bouldering zone, with a roof low enough to climb beneath. The climbing is steep, powerful and juggy. Eleven problems range from V4 through V11, with a solid block of V4s and V7s plus several in the double digits, so it suits people already climbing in the middle grades or harder. The cave stays shaded and cool even through the summer heat, making it a hot-weather refuge from the Las Vegas valley. The trail down is short but steep, losing about 300 feet.
nv_main_cave.approach: A short, steep trail loses roughly 300 feet on the way down. The cave is the first one reached, on the right where the path levels out.

nv_rainbow_mountain_east_face.blurb: A sandstone wall on the east side of Rainbow Mountain above Oak Creek Canyon in Red Rock, west of Las Vegas. Eleven routes, almost all trad with one bolted line, from about 5.8 to 5.11, and most sit around 5.10. Several are multi-pitch. Wide cracks line the base of the wall. The climbing is good but visits are occasional, so expect an adventurous, uncrowded feel. A faint trail with a few cairns peels off the main canyon trail to reach the base.
